sources.title: RFC 8493: The BagIt File Packaging Format, version 1.0
sources.observed_operation: Read-only web open/find of official RFC Editor page
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: BagIt v1.0 requires a payload manifest listing every payload file exactly once; complete requires listed files and each payload file listed; valid additionally requires every manifest checksum to verify. SHA-256 and SHA-512 support is required; SHA-512 creation default is a SHOULD, not an owner mandate. Payload-Oxum only quickly detects incomplete bags and cannot replace checksum validation. Direct file access is part of the layout. The RFC describes strong integrity but says BagIt is not designed against active attacks. Its filename section documents case, Unicode normalization, path-separator and Windows path-limit differences; it recommends discouraging case-only collisions, preventing names that differ only by normalization, and comparing manifest/filesystem names after applying the same normalization form.
sources.applicability: Strong fit for simple, filesystem-readable, immutable exhibition deposits; corrected versions need registrar-maintained identity/version relations outside a bag's fixity guarantee.

sources.title: Oxford Common File Layout Specification v1.1
sources.locator: §§3.1, 3.3–3.7, 3.8, 5.2; especially object structure and immutability, inventory id/head/manifest/versions, inventory digest, logs; lines 137–167, 189–211, 229–270, 289–310
sources.observed_operation: Read-only web open/find of version-pinned official spec
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Object identity must remain stable across versions; versions are sequential v1, v2… directories and existing version directories are intended immutable. Inventory records digest-to-path manifests, version states, a head, and its own digest sidecar. Root inventory is mandatory; per-version inventories are SHOULD; a logs directory is optional and log format is out of scope. SHA-512 appears in the example, not as a universal mandate in this research.
sources.applicability: Credible richer versioned-object alternative with transparent files and history; more structural and operational rules than a few gallery deposits.

sources.title: OCFL Specification v1.1 Change Log
sources.locator: Changes from v1.0 to v1.1; additions/clarifications including prior-version immutability and monotonic spec numbering (issue #544), UTF-8 inventory, contentDirectory direct-child clarification, stable id clarification (issues #514/#530/#542)
sources.observed_operation: Read-only web open of official version-pinned change log
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: v1.1 is described as a minor update focused on correction, clarification, and backwards-compatible prior-version conformance rules; it is not a claim that earlier objects are automatically repaired.
sources.applicability: Shows why released version and validator support matter when adopting a layout, and highlights version immutability and identifier continuity as explicit behaviors.

sources.title: Library of Congress bagit-python issue #51: validation warnings related to diacritics
sources.released_version_or_commit: Issue opened 2016-01-20; milestone 1.6; fix referenced by commits and closed after resolution
sources.locator: Issue body and comments describing Mac-created/copy-to-transfer-server path mismatch; comments on composed/decomposed accents and fix discussion, especially lines 161–168, 197–212, 271–298, 329–381
sources.observed_operation: Read-only web open of public issue and discussion
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The report says a bag passed on Mac but path validation on a Linux transfer server emitted manifest-missing and filesystem-unlisted warnings for visually equivalent accented names. The thread identifies Unicode normalization as the issue; fast Payload-Oxum success did not imply full path/fixity validation success.
sources.applicability: Direct evidence that ordinary file-tree copies across OS/filesystem environments can trigger path-level false mismatches; qualify real path behavior and review normalization collisions.

sources.title: bagit-python fix commit 16f34b6: Apply Unicode NFD normalization to filenames
sources.locator: Commit message, normalization of encoded/decoded manifest names and test that renames decomposed to composed filename and still validates; lines 129–145, 180–219, 239–250
sources.observed_operation: Read-only web open of exact public code commit
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: This implementation chose NFD normalization for path comparisons/read/write to accommodate OS/filesystem/archive behavior; that is implementation behavior, not a universal BagIt rule or license to rewrite gallery originals.
sources.applicability: Provides a concrete path-fix precedent and suggests testing validator release behavior on the actual copy/restore environments.

sources.locator: compare_manifests_with_fs and payload path handling; code lines 2677–2712 and normalization/conflict helpers around lines 3496–3572

sources.title: PREMIS Data Dictionary for Preservation Metadata, version 3.0
sources.locator: PREMIS v3.0 PDF, introduction/data model pp. 6–7 and §1.5.2 fixity pp. 58–59 (PDF pages 15–16, 67–69); special topic “Fixity, integrity, authenticity” pp. 258–259 (PDF pages 267–268), especially lines 6069–6090 in PDF text
sources.observed_operation: Read-only web search/open of official Library of Congress PDF record and excerpt
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The v3.0 PDF says equal digests calculated with the same algorithm at two points indicate no byte change during that interval. It records the fixity act/date as an Event and its result as eventOutcome. The same PDF explicitly says this procedure does not address object integrity or authenticity; PREMIS treats integrity checking as another event. This is a data dictionary, not a gallery-ready application.
sources.applicability: Shape a lightweight event log for person/time/action/tool/outcome while explicitly not claiming the digest proves custody or authorship.

sources.title: PREMIS 3.0 hierarchical listing of semantic units
sources.locator: Official v3.0 hierarchical listing lines 8–9 (page introduction), 100–140 (Event and Agent units: eventIdentifier/type/dateTime/outcome, linking agent/object, agentIdentifier/name/type/version and linking event)
sources.observed_operation: Read-only web search/open of official Library of Congress page
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The current HTML introduction describes five entities including Intellectual Entities, while the 2015 v3.0 PDF model text describes four (Objects, Events, Agents, Rights). The proposal only borrows listed Event/Agent fields, avoids claiming which page phrasing governs conformance, and does not claim a CSV implements PREMIS XML/schema.
sources.applicability: Supports a low-complexity actor/time/action/outcome custody record with explicit conformance limits.
